summary: LLM inference costs are the defining paradox of 2026: per-token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API spend passed $8.4 billion and continues to double as usage explodes. Stacking the five core optimization levers — prompt caching, model routing, prompt compression, output length control, and monitoring — routinely cuts total API spend by 60-80% with no loss in output quality. The single highest-leverage move is prompt caching, which saves 45-90% on repeated prompt prefixes while also improving time-to-first-token by 13-31%.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (prefix/KV caching)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated, static prompt prefix (e.g. a large system prompt or few-shot examples) so the model doesn't reprocess them on every call. The saving is structural, not a quality trade-off. Key discipline: keep the static portion at the front and dynamic content (tool results, user input) at the end, since naive full-context caching can paradoxically increase latency when dynamic data is cached.
techniques.savings: 45-90% reduction on cached input tokens; TTFT improves 13-31%
techniques.example: Place your 10,000-token system prompt and few-shot examples before the variable user query; Anthropic's cache_control marker on the static prefix then bills subsequent calls at ~10% of the normal input rate for the cached portion.

techniques.name: Model Routing (tiered model selection)
techniques.description: Classify each request by difficulty and route easy/high-volume tasks to cheap budget-tier models, reserving flagship models only for genuinely hard tasks. Flagship models charge $2-3/M input and $10-15/M output, while budget tiers can be 16x cheaper for identical token counts.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini / GPT-3.5-class models, 25% to a mid-tier model, and only 5% of the hardest queries to GPT-4-class, cutting the blended cost while keeping quality on complex requests.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed by the meaning (embedding similarity) of a query rather than exact text match, so paraphrased but semantically identical questions hit the cache. Best deployed as part of a multi-tier strategy: exact-match cache first, then semantic cache for near-duplicates.
techniques.savings: 40-50% cache hit rate; ~47% spend reduction when combined with budget-aware routing
works_with: any provider (provider-agnostic, sits in front of the API)
techniques.example: Using Redis or GPTCache with an embedding model, the queries 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset steps?' both resolve to the same cached answer, avoiding a second API call.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Shortens prompts by removing redundancy, pruning low-information tokens, trimming boilerplate, and compressing retrieved context (e.g. with LLMLingua-style compression) while preserving meaning. Attacks the input-token side of the bill directly.
techniques.example: Run retrieved RAG chunks through LLMLingua to drop filler tokens before injecting them, reducing a 4,000-token context to ~2,400 tokens with negligible answer-quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Constrain generation length via max_tokens, explicit instructions ('answer in one sentence'), and structured/JSON output to avoid verbose padding. Output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens, so this is disproportionately valuable.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and prompt 'Respond with a JSON object only, no explanation' to stop the model from emitting a paragraph of preamble before the answer.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Group non-latency-sensitive requests and submit them through a provider's asynchronous batch API, which offers steep discounts for jobs that can tolerate delayed completion (typically within 24 hours).
techniques.example: Send overnight document-summarization jobs via OpenAI's Batch API at 50% off standard per-token pricing instead of calling the synchronous endpoint during the day.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Cost Observability
techniques.description: Instrument every call to track token usage, cost per feature/user, cache hit rates, and model mix. Without monitoring you can't see which prompts are bloated or which route is leaking spend — it is the lever that makes the other four effective and sustainable.
techniques.savings: 10-30% indirectly, by surfacing waste and regressions
techniques.example: Pipe all requests through Helicone or Langfuse to get per-endpoint cost dashboards and alerts when average tokens-per-request spikes after a prompt change.

techniques.name: RAG / Retrieval over Long Context
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing an entire document corpus into the prompt, retrieve only the top-k relevant chunks via vector search. This keeps input token counts small and bounded rather than scaling with document size.
works_with: any provider (paired with a vector DB)
techniques.example: Rather than passing a 200-page manual (~150k tokens) each query, retrieve the 5 most relevant passages (~3k tokens) and inject only those.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer for LLM apps; caches responses by embedding similarity to cut duplicate calls and latency, with pluggable vector stores and embedding backends.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, Apache-2.0); self-hosted infra costs only

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that exposes 100+ LLM providers via one OpenAI-compatible API, with built-in model routing, fallbacks, caching, rate limiting, and spend tracking — ideal for cost-aware routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source core free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, admin UI, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing per-request cost/token logging, caching, rate limiting, and dashboards via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo, usage-based scaling

tools.name: Redis (Semantic Cache / LangCache)
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector-search and semantic caching capabilities; supports exact-match plus semantic caching tiers for low-latency LLM response reuse.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis open source free; Redis Cloud free tier then usage-based, from ~$5/mo upward

tools.name: LangChain / LangGraph
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations, prompt management, retrieval (RAG) tooling, and model abstractions useful for applying compression and routing patterns.
tools.pricing_paid: Framework free (open source); LangSmith observability from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt-compression toolkit that prunes low-information tokens from prompts and retrieved context, achieving large input-token reductions with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, cost/token analytics, prompt management, and evaluation — strong for cost observability and monitoring.
tools.pricing_paid: Self-hosted free; Langfuse Cloud free hobby tier, paid plans from ~$29/mo

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering routing, semantic caching, load balancing, fallbacks, and observability across providers through a single API endpoint.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/mo, usage-based

quick_wins: Turn on prompt caching for your large static system prompts and few-shot examples — move all static content to the front of the prompt to cut repeated input costs by 45-90%.
Set max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise or output JSON only; since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens, trimming verbosity is fast money.
Add a cheap-model router: send the bulk of easy/high-volume queries to a budget-tier model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and reserve flagship models for the hard 5-10%.
Drop a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to catch repeated and paraphrased queries — common chatbot workloads see 40-50% hit rates.
Instrument every call with Helicone or Langfuse so you can see per-feature token/cost usage and immediately catch bloated prompts or routing leaks.
